reading.body:
Kirsten Chadwick is named on 85 AI lobbying filings, and the client list runs from chipmakers and cloud vendors to media, film, and insurance.

The pattern is breadth rather than depth. No client appears on more than 14 of the 85 filings, and most appear on one to four. The largest counts belong to the Recording Industry Association of America and the News Media Alliance, both of which have spent years arguing about how their copyrighted work is used to train models. TSMC Arizona, Cisco, Siemens, Oracle, and Anthropic appear alongside them, which puts chip fabrication, networking, enterprise software, and a frontier model developer in the same portfolio. Siemens Energy is the one client on the list whose business is power equipment, and it appears on four filings.

The bills named are HR 6875, S 4456, HR 7757, S 2750, and S 3150, all from 2025 or later. The data does not say what any of them would do, so the filings establish that AI legislation is being lobbied but not which provisions drew the attention. The two disclosed prior government positions, at the Department of Education and in White House legislative affairs, are the kind of staffing background that lobbying disclosures require and that firms hire for.

What the data does not cover is outcome. It records who was named on which filing and for which client, not what was asked for, what was spent, or what happened to the bills. It also cannot show whether the AI label on a filing reflects a client's core interest or a single mention inside a broader lobbying report.

summary: Kirsten Chadwick is named as a lobbyist on 85 Lobbying Disclosure Act filing(s) about AI held by this site. The firms, clients and AI bills on those filings are below. LDA lobbyist id 61343. A different lobbyist with the same name has a separate page.
